featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been a member of Youmania Gym and feel it is important to share my experience.

For the past 2–3 months, the gym has been facing persistent air-conditioning issues. Despite raising the concern multiple times with the reception staff, the problem remained unresolved for an extended period. As a paying member, I expect basic facilities to be maintained, especially in a gym where people are exercising intensely.

What was particularly disappointing was the response from the management. Instead of focusing on resolving the issue, I was questioned for expressing my dissatisfaction. During the discussion, one of the owners suggested that people use treadmills to sweat, implying that proper cooling and ventilation were not necessary. This completely misses the point. Members come to work out, not to train in uncomfortable and poorly ventilated conditions.

Technical issues can happen in any business. What matters is how quickly they are addressed and how management responds to customer feedback. Unfortunately, the prolonged AC problem combined with the dismissive attitude toward legitimate concerns made for a disappointing experience.

I hope the management prioritizes member comfort, resolves maintenance issues promptly, and treats customer feedback with greater professionalism in the future.

The situation became so frustrating that I chose not to utilize the final month of my membership and stopped attending the gym altogether. As someone who values fitness and trains regularly, I found the environment uncomfortable and unsuitable for effective workouts.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Muscle Cage Fitness, Goregaon today through Fitpass, and honestly, it was my worst gym experience so far (and I’ve been to quite a few via Fitpass).

First off, the shoe policy makes zero sense. Okay, I get that outside shoes aren’t allowed, but what if someone only has one pair and brings them in a clean bag just for the gym? They’re still “outside shoes” technically, but clean. It just felt like rules for the sake of rules.

The moment I entered, there was a pungent smell in the gym—definitely not the welcoming vibe you’d expect. Then they asked me my workout duration upfront (??). Never in my life has a gym asked me how long I plan to stay.

Apparently, my pass only covers 90 mins, which was fine, but the way they asked was just uncomfortable.
Next, when I got on the treadmill, I was told there’s a 10-minute limit for cardio. Like… what?? This isn’t some luxury gym with a line of people waiting, so why are there these weird restrictions?

To top it off, there were only two trainers, neither helpful nor approachable. Honestly, they seemed inexperienced and uninterested. The vibe was off from the second I walked in—whispering among themselves, unprofessional, and honestly gave me awkward, negative energy.

Overall: strange rules, bad smell, poor staff vibes, and not worth the visit. Definitely not going again.

The management seems efficient only when it comes to collecting money, but completely indifferent when members raise genuine concerns. Despite multiple complaints, no corrective action is taken. Ironically, when payments are due, the manager named Yash is extremely persistent, calling and messaging repeatedly, which feels harassing.

Overall, I would not recommend this gym unless the management takes serious steps to renovate the facility, maintain equipment properly, ensure basic amenities, and hire sufficient trainers.

Gym Creed – Charkop Branch

There is almost zero management. Only one or two staff members seem to pay attention; the rest appear uninterested in what’s happening in the gym. Member issues are not taken seriously.

The gym setup is slightly better compared to some other local gyms, but maintenance is a major problem.
If a machine breaks down, it takes 2–3 months to get repaired — this is from my personal experience.

4. Cleanliness Issues
Cleanliness is inconsistent. Some days the floors smell, and the washrooms are poorly maintained and often stink. This reflects a lack of regular cleaning standards.

5. Low Energy Environment
The overall energy of the gym feels dull and uninspiring. There is no motivating atmosphere for members.

Overall Verdict:
Gym Creed in Charkop has potential but suffers from poor management, lack of maintenance, hygiene issues, and low-quality environment. Not recommended unless major improvements are made.
